name: Daylight Ops
tagline: The command center at 9am — crisp paper-white surfaces, cobalt conviction.
rationale: This is the direct answer to "it was all black": a layered cool-gray light theme in the Linear/Stripe dashboard idiom, built for boardroom projectors and daytime ops shifts. Depth comes from a cool #f3f5f8 canvas holding pure-white panels with hairline edges and soft slate shadows — never sterile flat white. One confident deep-cobalt accent carries every interactive signal (buttons, focus, nav-active, brand mark), with a restrained deep teal as the secondary telemetry voice, so the interface reads decisive rather than colorful. Every text and chip pairing is verified at WCAG AA or better on both the white panels and the gray canvas.
pitch: You told us the first pass felt "all black" — this one is the opposite pole, and it's the safest room to walk a CFO into. White panels on a cool-gray field, deep slate text at print-grade contrast, and a single cobalt blue doing all the talking: it reads like the tools your advertisers already trust with money — Stripe, Linear — which makes Vantage's numbers feel bankable by association. Every campaign map, payout table, and fraud flag stays legible on a sunlit laptop or a conference-room projector, and it photographs beautifully in decks.

tokens.atmosphere: radial-gradient(60% 50% at 70% 0%, rgb(30 80 210 / 0.06), transparent 70%), radial-gradient(50% 40% at 12% 100%, rgb(15 118 110 / 0.05), transparent 70%), #f3f5f8

componentNotes: On-accent text: pure #ffffff on cobalt buttons (6.7:1; the existing `text-bg` mapping is replaced by explicit white — verify the utility resolves to #ffffff, and white on accentSoft is 8.3:1). Hover direction inverts for light mode — accentSoft (#1a43b8) is DARKER than accent, so `hover:bg-accent-soft` (mapped to accentSoft; confirm this class exists in the component layer — the old amber-era `hover:bg-amber-soft` name is retired) correctly deepens on hover. Glow shadows are soft colored elevation below the element with alpha capped at ~0.25–0.28 — never radial halos and never heavier than Stripe/Linear light-mode buttons. Surface stacking: raised (#e9eef5) is a tinted INSET used only inside white panels (ghost buttons, nav-active, default chips); it must never render directly on the bg canvas. Overlays (dropdown menus, popovers, tooltips) use panel #ffffff + edgeStrong #c2cbd9 border + a doubled shadowPanel — never raised; re-point the timeseries tooltip from raised/95 to #ffffff at 97% opacity with border #c2cbd9. Chips keep the 10%-tint + token-text formula — verified on tint-over-white: accent 5.8:1, secondary 4.8:1, success 4.9:1, danger 5.3:1, amber #aa4f09 4.7:1 (all ≥4.5:1). Contrast audit (verified): ink 15.9:1 panel / 14.6:1 bg / 13.6:1 raised; muted 7.5:1 panel / 6.9:1 bg; faint #657185 4.9:1 panel / 4.5:1 bg (AA — safe for axis and helper text); accent-as-text 6.7:1 panel / 6.1:1 bg. Danger red #be123c is reserved for danger semantics only — it never appears in the categorical chart palette (series 5 is fuchsia #a21caf instead); all six chart colors hold ≥4.4:1 on panel and bg with clear lightness steps between cobalt/violet and cobalt/slate for CVD viewers. Timeseries hardcodes dark-theme hex (#262a33 grid, #5a6071 axis text, #eaedf2 direct label, #121419 hover-dot stroke) — re-point those four SVG attribute values at gridLine / faint / ink / panel tokens for the swap; faint now passes AA so axis text maps to it directly. Set `color-scheme: light` in @layer base. Panel border stays 1px edge + shadowPanel (borders carry the structure; shadows are whisper-soft). Theme signatures — do not omit: (1) gridLine rgb(26 34 51 / 0.045) renders as a faint blueprint grid on the bg canvas behind map and chart panels; (2) secondary teal #0f766e owns all live-telemetry accents — KPI-tile sparklines, the live-status dot, streaming row highlights — cobalt never appears in passive data. DEEPENED (routes): the cobalt panel top-rule gains an origin terminus dot (8px white disc, 2px cobalt ring, at left:16px/top:-5px; panels get position:relative).

name: Ivory Ledger
tagline: Naira paper — banknote engraving, espresso ink, one heirloom terracotta.
rationale: The client's objection was "all black," so the strongest counter-offer is the full opposite pole done with conviction: warm porcelain surfaces and near-black espresso ink at print-grade contrast (14.1:1 on the page ground, 16.1:1 on panels), not the pale gray of default SaaS. Terracotta replaces amber in the primary accent slot — it keeps the brand's warm signal hue but reads heirloom rather than hazard, and at #a63d17 it carries ivory button text at 5.2:1. Petrol teal (secondary), forest green (success) and madder red (danger) are all deepened to 5.7–7:1 on paper so chips and stat tones work as tinted letterpress marks instead of neon. The full text ramp is AA-verified on every surface: ink, muted (7.0:1 on panel) and faint (5.2:1 on panel, 4.55:1 on the deepened bg) all clear 4.5:1, and the bg sits a full step below the paper panels so the sheets-on-desk elevation survives a washed-out projector. Glows become soft colored elevation shadows, which is the correct light-theme translation of the existing glow vocabulary.
pitch: You told us the current build felt "all black" — this is its daylight twin, and it's the one that will make Vantage look like a company, not a tool. Ivory Ledger borrows from print, not from dashboards: bone-paper panels, espresso ink, terracotta as the single signature accent, the same live map and campaign flows now reading like a premium annual report. Advertisers see it in a boardroom at 2pm and it looks like money well spent; your ops team still gets every signal color, every chip, every chart — just typeset instead of backlit.

tokens.atmosphere: radial-gradient(60% 50% at 72% 0%, rgb(166 61 23 / 0.07), transparent 70%), radial-gradient(50% 40% at 10% 100%, rgb(30 95 90 / 0.05), transparent 70%), #efe9d8

componentNotes: On-accent button text: keep the existing `text-bg` mapping — bg (#efe9d8, warm ivory) on accent #a63d17 gives 5.2:1, and hover (accentSoft #8c3512) DARKENS rather than lightens, the correct light-theme press feel, at 6.6:1. Panels sit LIGHTER than the bg (paper sheets on a warm desk, 1.14:1 lift) with raised = pure white; hairline warm borders (edge/edgeStrong) carry the structure and shadows stay soft and brown-tinted, never gray. All three glow slots are converted to two-layer colored elevation shadows (tight contact shadow + soft falloff) — do not ship dark halo glows on light paper. StatusChip tone tints (color/10 backgrounds, color/40 borders) work unchanged because all four signal colors are deep (5.7–7:1 as text on panel) — they read as letterpress ink stamps. TEXT RAMP: ink → muted (#5c5449, 7.0:1 panel) → faint (#736756, 5.2:1 panel / 4.55:1 bg) — all three tiers pass AA on every surface; use faint only for tertiary captions and timestamps. CHART TEXT: axis ticks and timestamps are load-bearing — route them at var(--color-muted), NOT faint; the timeseries components currently hardcode dark-theme hex values for grid (#262a33), tick text (#5a6071), last-point label (#eaedf2) and tooltip point stroke (#121419) — these must be re-pointed at var(--color-edge)/muted/ink/panel tokens for any second theme to work. CHART PALETTE ORDER IS CVD-DELIBERATE (terracotta, petrol, violet, olive, blue, warm gray): every adjacent pair carries a ≥1.5:1 luminance separation and the red-green-confusable pairs (terracotta/olive, petrol/gray) are non-adjacent — do not reorder or re-darken series 3 (#8a5aa5) or series 6 (#73736a), both sit at 4.5+:1 on panel. MAP: a stock cool-gray light basemap will read as a cold rectangle inside the warm chrome — prefer a custom warm style (land #efe9d8, roads #fbf8f0, water rgb(30 95 90 / 0.25)); if a stock light style must ship, apply filter: sepia(0.18) saturate(0.9) to the map canvas. Bg-grid utility should use gridLine (ink at 5%) instead of white lines. Focus ring and ::selection follow accent automatically and both pass on ivory. DEEPENED (naira paper): body carries a guilloché lattice (interlocking-circles SVG data-URI, terracotta at 5.5% stroke-opacity, 120px tile) under the grain — banknote security-print.

name: Blue Hour
tagline: Adire night — the city twenty minutes after sunset, dyed in Abeokuta indigo. Never black.
rationale: The complaint was "all black," not "too dark" — ops rooms run dark monitors for a reason, and Vantage is an ops surface. So every neutral in this theme carries real blue chroma: the background is a deep indigo-navy (#161f47) saturated enough to survive a dimmed boardroom projector, panels step up in both lightness and blue chroma (raised nudges toward indigo-violet), and the grid/hairlines are blue-tinted rather than white-on-black. The accent pair — sodium-streetlight gold against ice blue — is literally the palette of a city at blue hour, which is where vehicle-mounted ads live. It keeps the existing brand's warm-primary DNA (gold inherits the amber slot cleanly) while making the whole frame feel dimensional and alive.
pitch: You told us the product felt all black — you're right, and the fix isn't white backgrounds. Blue Hour keeps the low-glare dark canvas your ops team will be staring at for eight-hour shifts, but replaces black with the deep indigo of a city sky twenty minutes after sunset: every surface is visibly blue, panels layer with color instead of gray, and streetlight-gold and ice-blue accents give campaigns, maps, and earnings real luminous presence. It photographs beautifully in a boardroom and stays easy on the eyes in a night-shift ops room — the option that hears the feedback without giving up what dark does best.

tokens.atmosphere: radial-gradient(55% 45% at 78% -5%, rgb(255 182 72 / 0.10), transparent 65%), radial-gradient(45% 40% at 8% 100%, rgb(122 209 255 / 0.09), transparent 70%), radial-gradient(70% 60% at 40% 55%, rgb(52 74 138 / 0.22), transparent 75%), #161f47

componentNotes: RAMP (reconciled): the original #131c33 family was measurably a stock-Tailwind-slate clone that collapses to black on a dim projector — the whole ramp is lifted ~4-5 lightness points with more chroma (bg #161f47, panel #1d2a58, raised #2a3372 which also nudges toward indigo-violet so elevation genuinely shifts hue). Primary buttons keep text-bg on the accent: #161f47 on #ffb648 measures 9.1:1 — hover moves to accentSoft #ffc766, and the gold glow shadow stays (this is a dark theme; glows are correct and are the point). Verified contrast on the lifted ramp: ink 14.6:1 bg / 12.6:1 panel / 10.6:1 raised; muted 6.7:1 bg / 5.8:1 panel / 4.9:1 raised; faint #8794bd 4.6:1 panel, 5.3:1 bg (AA — reconciled up from #67759b which failed at 3.4:1). edgeStrong #5d77b0 (3.1:1 on panel) is the interactive-control boundary (inputs, focused chips); edge #31447e stays decorative-only. Panels stay border-first with the inset top highlight blue-tinted (rgb(148 178 255 / 0.07)) so edges shimmer indigo instead of gray. Chips keep the /10 tint + /40 border recipe — chip text verified: gold 7.9:1, ice 8.1:1, mint 8.0:1, danger 5.0:1 on panel. bg-grid switches from white 2.5% to the blue-tinted gridLine token so even empty canvas reads indigo, not black. MAP: stock dark tiles are graphite-black and would reintroduce the rejected black through the hero panel — overlay the tile layer with rgb(22 31 71 / 0.45) using mix-blend-mode: color so tiles inherit the navy hue (or ship a custom navy style: land #141d3c, water #0e1530, roads #2c3a5e, labels #9aa8c7). CHARTS: migrate hardcodes — grid #262a33 → chartGrid, tick fill #5a6071 → muted #9aa8c7 (ticks are load-bearing; faint is reserved for empty-state hints), last-point label #eaedf2 → ink, hover-dot stroke #121419 → panel #1d2a58. Palette reconciled for CVD: mint darkened to #35c27b (1.31:1 luminance gap vs gold, 6.0:1 on panel; the UI success token stays #57dd94 — they are deliberately decoupled), rose replaced with magenta-violet #e879d9 (~50° hue from danger so a neutral series can never read as an alert), series-6 slate #8ea0cf de-collided from the muted text token. Focus ring, selection, logo dot, and active-nav all follow the accent slot (gold) automatically. DEEPENED (adire night): an adire-eleko pattern (dot rows + resist dashes, #cfe0ff at 5% fill-opacity, 88px tile) layers over the atmosphere on body and at 7% on the sidebar glass.

name: Danfo
tagline: Lagos livery — the yellow-and-black of the city's own fleet, painted, not printed.
rationale: The direction only this product could wear: the visual language of Lagos transit itself. Danfo yellow is treated the way the buses treat it — as painted surface, never as text: the vivid #f7c400 lives on the livery band, the sidebar (yellow with a 3px black coachline), and primary buttons (enamel yellow, 2px painted black edge, hard 3px drop), while a deep ochre #7d6300 (5.7:1 on panel) holds the accent token slot so accent text, focus rings and chart leads stay WCAG-legal. Status chips become hand-cut cabin stickers: white, outlined 2px in their tone color, tilted -1.4°. Bricolage Grotesque keeps display type warm and characterful rather than corporate.
pitch: Instantly local, instantly yours — no competitor can wear this livery credibly. It reads as the city itself.
componentNotes: Verified WCAG (computed): ink 16.2:1 bg / 18.3:1 panel; muted #57503f 8.0:1 panel, 4.9:1 on the yellow sidebar (idle nav labels); faint 5.6:1 panel / 5.0:1 bg; ochre accent-as-text 5.7:1 panel / 5.1:1 bg (also the focus ring, ≥3:1 everywhere); secondary blue 8.9:1; success 6.5:1; danger 6.5:1; ink-on-yellow surfaces 11.2:1. Signature rules (globals.css): livery band body::before (yellow with twin black stripes); aside.bg-panel wears #f7c400 + 3px #17150f coachline, active nav inverts to black-on-yellow, aside .text-amber snaps to ink; span.micro.rounded-full chips become white stickers with 2px currentColor outline, 8px radius, rotate(-1.4deg); primary buttons repaint to #f7c400/ink/2px ink border with 0 3px 0 ink drop, hover deepens to #e8b800 (the unlayered rule outranks the utility hover so amber-soft never shows), active translates 2px with 1px drop. Replaced the Prism direction entirely — it was a colorway with no product identity.

name: Hi-Vis
tagline: Concrete, ink, and one blaze of safety orange — the ops floor in daylight.
rationale: The client's objection was "all black," so this direction goes to the opposite pole without losing the product's operational seriousness: warm concrete off-whites, near-black ink at 14:1+ contrast, and a single blaze-orange accent used the way road crews use it — sparingly and decisively. Elevation moves from glows to crisp near-black hairline borders (edge-strong snaps to ink on hover/tooltips), which suits the existing Swiss-grid layout, mono eyebrows, and IBM Plex Mono microcopy far better than soft shadows would. The one-accent discipline also makes status colors (cobalt, signal green, signal red) read instantly against neutral surfaces — exactly what fraud/ops monitoring needs.
pitch: Hi-Vis is the daylight shift of your control room: paper-white panels on warm concrete, near-black type you can read across the room, and one unmistakable safety-orange signal on every primary action — the same visual language as the vests, cones, and vehicle wraps your business actually runs on. It photographs beautifully in advertiser decks and sales demos where dark UIs turn to mud on projectors, and it makes anomalies — an open fraud flag, a stalled campaign — impossible to miss because color only ever means something. If you want Vantage to feel like precision industrial hardware instead of a gamer dashboard, this is the one.
componentNotes: ACCENT (reconciled): #FF5C00 failed the 3:1 non-text floor on both surfaces (2.46:1 bg / 2.84:1 panel) — the accent is now #E04E00 (3.17:1 bg, 3.66:1 panel), which doubles as the chart lead so the focus ring is legal everywhere. ON-ACCENT TEXT: buttons use ink (#131310) on the accent, not text-bg — black-on-blaze-orange is the safety-signage idiom, verified 4.66:1 (the light bg would fail at ~2.3:1); same for the skip-link and any solid-accent fill. accentSoft #DB4E00 is the darkened hover (ink text 4.52:1) — the step is subtle, so hover also lifts glowAccent slightly to make the state unmistakable; light themes darken on hover, never lighten. STAT TONES (corrected claim): the old spec's assertion that accent numerals 'clear 3:1' was false at 2.84:1 — with #E04E00 at 3.66:1 on panel, 30px+ numerals now genuinely pass large-text; hero KPIs still default to ink, accent tone is reserved for the one number that matters. BORDERS OVER SHADOWS: edge #C6C2B8 is a visible warm hairline on every Panel; edgeStrong is full ink, so ghost-button hover and tooltips snap to a ruled black outline — that snap IS the elevation language; shadowPanel stays whisper-quiet. Interactive-control borders (inputs, selects) must not rely on edge alone (1.63:1) — use #8F8A7B (3.16:1 on panel, same warm hue) or edgeStrong. CHIPS: accent-tone StatusChips flip to solid industrial-tag style (bg accent, ink text, no border); secondary/success/danger keep the tint pattern — all three clear 4.5:1 as text on panel (6.7/5.0/5.7). TEXT RAMP: muted #5B584F 6.5:1 panel; faint reconciled to #6B675D (5.2:1 panel, 4.5:1 bg — the old #8A867B failed at 3.3:1); reserve faint for tertiary captions. CHARTS: swap timeseries hardcodes — grid #262a33 → chartGrid, tick fill #5a6071 → muted #5B584F (ticks are load-bearing), last-value label #eaedf2 → ink, hover-dot stroke #121419 → #FFFFFF; area-fill gradient opacity drops to 0.18→0.02 on white. Palette reconciled for semantics + CVD: status-green removed from the categorical set (success/danger are status-only, never series colors) — slot 3 is dark ochre #8A6D00 (4.5:1 panel), purple lifted to #B052D6 (1.76:1 luminance gap vs cobalt), teal #0E8FB0 (1.31:1 gap vs ochre). ATMOSPHERE: one decisive orange wash (0.14 alpha) instead of two timid corners — two tinted corners read as decoration, one reads as intent; gridLine bumped to 0.06 so the Swiss grid does the structural work. bg-grid inverts to the dark gridLine value. Set color-scheme: light on :root; focus ring accent #E04E00 passes 3:1 on all surfaces; selection tint follows the accent. DEEPENED (fleet/tarmac): h1 gets a 4px road centre-line (repeating ink dashes, 132px) under 12px padding; default-tone chips (span.micro.rounded-full.text-muted) take the number-plate idiom — white, 2px ink frame, registration blue #1a3ba5 (9.5:1), 0.14em tracking.
